memory_update.text: LOPE is the primary reference name for this node because it explicitly provides outsourced university enrollment, marketing, counseling, compliance, LMS, SIS, and student-lifecycle services.

ATGE and PRDO should remain in the underfollowed lane as direct student-funnel owners where employer-channel exposure and compliant advising workflows may matter more if AI weakens generic search-led acquisition.

NNI is a second-order infrastructure candidate: education payments, financial-aid workflow, SIS, enrollment services, and student-loan servicing may be overlooked because the company is not usually categorized as an enrollment-operations vendor.
Need primary-source verification for employer-originated starts, CAC, paid-search dependence, AI-search impact, enrollment-conversion metrics, and retention outcomes across LOPE, ATGE, PRDO, and NNI.
LOPE should remain a high-priority candidate for this node because supplied evidence directly links employer partnerships, online/hybrid enrollment growth, and AI-driven changes in student discovery.

NNI is an underfollowed infrastructure candidate: verify whether Education Technology Services and Payments is meaningfully tied to higher-ed enrollment, payments, communications, and student lifecycle workflows.
The node may be less about generic lead generation and more about employer-channel distribution, compliant servicing/payment rails, lifecycle communications, and proprietary advising data.

This pass lacks direct sourced evidence for CRM vendors, call-center/advising outsourcers, AI-search-optimization vendors, and listed marketing agencies serving universities; follow-up searches should target those supplier categories specifically.
LOPE should be tracked as an underfollowed enrollment-operations and employer-channel infrastructure candidate, not only as an education services operator.
STRA has direct evidence of employer-channel and education-benefits infrastructure through Workforce Edge, Sophia Learning, and employer-affiliated enrollment metrics.
NNI is a second-order campus workflow candidate; exposure is less direct but may matter if payment friction, retention, and financial engagement become enrollment-conversion chokepoints.

Need a separate pass for private enrollment CRM/advising vendors and public large-cap CRM context anchors such as Salesforce or HubSpot, but they were intentionally not prioritized in this underfollowed small/mid-cap pass.

LOPE should remain the reference name for employer-channel enrollment infrastructure because provided evidence directly links it to large-scale educational agreements, online/hybrid growth, and employer-sourced student starts.

NNI enters the underfollowed lane as an education payments, servicing, communications, and workflow infrastructure hypothesis; verify whether ETSP has admissions/enrollment relevance or is mainly back-office payments and administration.

The public-market map for admissions CRM and enrollment conversion is thin because many obvious assets appear private or embedded inside broader software companies; later layers should search for public CRM, call-center, student-success analytics, and compliance-workflow vendors with explicit university customers.

The strongest chokepoint signal to track is the mix shift from paid search and generic lead generation toward employer relationships, owned advising channels, high-intent program data, and compliant student lifecycle workflows.

summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Expanded the direct public-company universe for the node around student acquisition, enrollment operations, advising, employer-channel enrollment, and compliant education workflows. The strongest direct exposure appears in mid-cap education service/platform operators that either manage the enrollment funnel for university partners or own large online/adult-learning student funnels. This pass separates reference leaders from an underfollowed discovery lane; no buy/sell view is implied. Expanded a narrow universe around the node where higher-education demand generation may shift away from generic paid-search lead flow toward employer channels, proprietary advising workflows, compliant enrollment operations, program data, payments, and student-success infrastructure. The strongest evidence in the supplied context points to Grand Canyon Education as a reference/underfollowed hybrid because employer partnerships and enrollment operations are directly visible. Nelnet is a second-order infrastructure candidate through education technology services, payments, software, and servicing systems. Stride is included as a reference education platform with lifelong-learning and workforce-training exposure. A fourth shadow candidate, Perdoceo Education, is included only as a speculative public-market proxy for adult online enrollment operations because no direct supporting source was supplied in this pass.
